title: Mailjet Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Add-Ons
summary: Mailjet pricing's base plan cost is just the entry fee; your actual cost scales with email volume. Understand the real price before selecting a tier.
body_markdown:
## Keep Mailjet contact lists in sync with Activepieces


Your contact count is the one part of Mailjet's bill you control, and that is where Activepieces, an automation tool that connects apps through trigger-and-action flows, helps: its Free plan costs $0 and allows unlimited flows, so the sync adds no line to your budget.


Since contact count is one of the gates that moves you up a tier, a list full of dead addresses is a cost you're choosing to carry.


### Which Mailjet contact tasks to automate


Three sources tend to create the mess: a web form, a CRM (the system where your sales team keeps customer records), and a shop's order system.


With 746 integrations to draw on, Activepieces lets each of them feed one flow that writes to a single Mailjet contact list, so you can consolidate contact data from hundreds of different sources.


Every change in a source system becomes one matching change on the list, with no manual export in between.


The practical value is the remove arrow. A form signup adds a contact, a CRM edit updates a name or a tag, and an unsubscribe or a cancelled account removes or flags the record.


Without that last step, people who left months ago still count toward your contact total, and **you pay to email nobody** .


The same logic cuts duplicates. When the form, the CRM and the shop each create their own entry for one person, a flow that checks for an existing contact before adding keeps you from counting that person more than once.


### What it does not change


Activepieces doesn't alter Mailjet's pricing, raise its daily send cap, or unlock a feature your plan gates. Its own side of the bill is small: a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, and the Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month.


It only keeps the contact side of the equation honest. If your real volume lands in a more expensive tier, a tidy list won't move you out of it.


It's also irrelevant if you send by hand.


A sender who uploads a list for an occasional campaign has no recurring sync to automate, and a flow would add a tool to maintain for no saving.


Price your plan on real volume first; automate only once contact churn is a recurring chore.
